title: bulk-upgrade-multi-lang-sdks-bump-deps-and-prune-legacy-api-params
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We will perform coordinated dependency upgrades across Python, JavaScript, and Go SDKs and remove/mark deprecated legacy API surface (old query params, legacy auth fields) that have accumulated technical debt. Goals are to reduce transitive vulnerabilities, adopt current LTS runtimes and packaging patterns, and simplify the public surface so we can more reliably support semantic versioning going forward.

Scope:
- Python SDK: bump to httpx 0.24, typing-extensions->latest, bump pydantic v1->v1.11 (no migration to v2 in this ticket), drop support for urllib3-specific shims, enable async-first codepaths by default where safe.
- JS SDK: target Node 18 LTS minimum, replace isomorphic-fetch with cross-fetch, remove deprecated client.createCompletion(... legacyParams) overload, switch build to ESM-first artifact.
- Go SDK: update go.mod modules to require go1.21, bump google/go-cmp and github.com/pkg/errors replacements, tidy up module graph to remove duplicate cryptography transitive deps.
- API surface: identify and document all deprecated query parameters and JSON fields (legacy_mode, use_legacy_auth, model_alias) and add deprecation headers in responses. Provide migration guide and automated codemod for JS and Python where feasible.

Acceptance criteria:
- All three SDKs compile and run CI smoke tests in runtime-1.22 image.
- No high or critical CVEs introduced; transitive CVE count reduced vs baseline.
- Deprecation warnings are visible for flagged API fields and documented in the migration guide.
- New SDK packages published to internal registry with release notes and migration snippets.
- Rollout plan and rollback steps documented in the ticket.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Inventory and baseline (done): ran dependency audit across mono-repos, created dependency matrix and CVE list. Snapshot: python: 7 medium CVEs (transitive), js: 4 medium CVEs, go: 2 medium CVEs.
2) Python changes: create branch eng/ENG-32641/python-deps, drop urllib3 shims, introduce httpx client adapter, add compatibility layer so user code using requests shim continues to work for two cycles. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/492
3) JS changes: branch eng/ENG-32641/js-esm, migrate to ESM bundling, replace fetch polyfills, remove legacy overloads behind 2-week feature flag and warn in console/log. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/1183
4) Go changes: branch eng/ENG-32641/go-mod-tidy, update go.mod to go1.21, run `go mod vendor` and CI. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/274
5) API deprecation: add header X-Redwood-Deprecation and structured body warning for requests using deprecated fields. Confluence migration guide created: https://confluence.internal/redwood/SDK-deprecation-migration-guide
6) QA & Canary: publish prerelease packages and run canary customers (internal services + 3 partner integrations) for 7 days. Monitor errors and client telemetry.

Risks & mitigations:
- Breaking user code: mitigate by compatibility shims and multi-cycle deprecation window, clear release notes, and offering a codemod for common JS/Python patterns.
- Build/regression flakiness: add additional unit tests around auth and streaming behaviors before merge; expand CI matrix to include Node 18/20 and Python 3.10/3.11.
- Unknown transitive CVE regressions: run Snyk/Depscan after each merge and hold on major transitive changes until triage.

Rollout and communication:
- Internal: send RFC and changelog to #sdk-updates, attach migration guide.
- External: blog post + changelog for customers; mark deprecated features in API docs with effective-deprecation-date and sunset-date (90 days).

Follow-ups:
- Post-rollout: schedule a follow-up ticket to track removal of compatibility shims (ENG-32641-RM) after 2 release cycles.
- Consider full pydantic v2 migration in a separate dedicated project (breaking).
